evidence.claim: Hu Jintao was unexpectedly escorted out of the 20th Party Congress closing ceremony while the congress unanimously advanced Xi's political vision.
evidence.title: Chinese ex-President Hu Jintao escorted out of party congress
evidence.excerpt: Hu Jintao was unexpectedly escorted out of the 20th Party Congress closing ceremony while the congress unanimously advanced Xi's political vision.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous coverage of a symbolic power-display event at the party congress.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly associated with Xi because the event occurred at his congress and underscored his dominance.
contrary_evidence: The exact reason for Hu's removal was not publicly explained.

evidence.claim: The CCP dictated the legislative agenda to the NPC, citizens could not freely choose the officials who governed them, the CCP controlled elections and appointments, and the NPC removed the two-term limit for president and vice president.
evidence.title: Human Rights Reports: Custom Report Excerpts - China
evidence.excerpt: The CCP dictated the legislative agenda to the NPC, citizens could not freely choose the officials who governed them, the CCP controlled elections and appointments, and the NPC removed the two-term limit for president and vice president.
evidence.source_locator: Section 3, Freedom to Participate in the Political Process
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official U.S. country report with explicit political-process findings and ruler-relevant institutional facts.
evidence.period_fit: Describes the 2022 institutional environment and its continuation into Xi's 2022 rule.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Xi's incumbency and the institutional rules that kept him in office.
contrary_evidence: County-level elections formally exist, but they are not free or competitive.

evidence.claim: Xi said the overarching goal in Xinjiang was social stability and lasting security, and that Islam in China must be Chinese in orientation.
evidence.title: Xi inspects Xinjiang
evidence.excerpt: Xi said the overarching goal in Xinjiang was social stability and lasting security, and that Islam in China must be Chinese in orientation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official transcript-like reporting of Xi's own remarks during a 2022 inspection tour.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct and personal: these are Xi's own stated objectives for Xinjiang policy.
contrary_evidence: Official framing does not show public consent or rights protection.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said Edmund Wan was sentenced for criticizing the government on radio and fundraising for young Hong Kong protesters, and that he was targeted merely for exercising peaceful expression.
evidence.title: Hong Kong: Veteran radio host sentenced for peaceful activism: Giggs Edmund Wan
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said Edmund Wan was sentenced for criticizing the government on radio and fundraising for young Hong Kong protesters, and that he was targeted merely for exercising peaceful expression.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct case-level reporting by a major human-rights organization on a specific peaceful-activity prosecution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi because Hong Kong's political freedom was sharply constrained under PRC sovereignty and the NSL framework during his rule.
contrary_evidence: Hong Kong authorities treated the case as lawful sedition and money-laundering enforcement.

evidence.claim: The Asia-Pacific analysis says China continues to extend its information-control model, describing absolute and autocratic control of information, and notes that Hong Kong suffered a steep drop in the 2022 index.
evidence.title: RSF's 2022 World Press Freedom Index: a new era of polarisation
evidence.excerpt: The Asia-Pacific analysis says China continues to extend its information-control model, describing absolute and autocratic control of information, and notes that Hong Kong suffered a steep drop in the 2022 index.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Index analysis from a specialized press-freedom NGO with a transparent methodology and consistent country coverage.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 index year and the same political environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi because the report directly attributes the information-control model to the PRC regime under his leadership.
contrary_evidence: RSF is an advocacy-oriented press-freedom organization, though its conclusions are method-driven.

evidence.claim: Opponents of the anti-COVID measures used dating apps and blocked social-media platforms to evade censors and police during the 2022 protest wave.
evidence.title: Dating apps and Telegram: How China protesters are defying authorities
evidence.excerpt: Opponents of the anti-COVID measures used dating apps and blocked social-media platforms to evade censors and police during the 2022 protest wave.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting based on contemporaneous observation of protester tactics and state controls.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and the late-2022 protest wave.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi because the censorship and police response were part of the national political environment under his rule.
contrary_evidence: This describes citizen circumvention efforts rather than a formal state policy memo.

evidence.claim: The CCP Central Committee oversees Tibet policies, no Tibetan members sat in the Politburo or Standing Committee, and the report lists forced disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, political prisoners, censorship and website blocking, and severe restrictions on peaceful assembly, religion, movement, and political participation.
evidence.title: Human Rights Reports: Custom Report Excerpts - China (includes Tibet, Hong Kong, and Macau) - Tibet
evidence.excerpt: The CCP Central Committee oversees Tibet policies, no Tibetan members sat in the Politburo or Standing Committee, and the report lists forced disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, political prisoners, censorship and website blocking, and severe restrictions on peaceful assembly, religion, movement, and political participation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official country report with explicit attribution of central control and documented abuses.
evidence.period_fit: Describes conditions in the 2022 reporting period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant because Tibet policy is centrally controlled and attributed to the CCP leadership under Xi.
contrary_evidence: Authorities justify these measures as security and anti-separatism policy.

evidence.claim: The PRC and SAR governments increasingly encroached on freedom of expression, including coerced closures of Apple Daily and Stand News, and used sedition and National Security Law charges against critics and protesters.
evidence.title: Human Rights Reports: Custom Report Excerpts - China (includes Tibet, Hong Kong, and Macau) - Hong Kong
evidence.excerpt: The PRC and SAR governments increasingly encroached on freedom of expression, including coerced closures of Apple Daily and Stand News, and used sedition and National Security Law charges against critics and protesters.
evidence.source_locator: Section 2, Respect for Civil Liberties, Freedom of Expression
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official country report with specific examples of media and protest repression in Hong Kong.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi because Hong Kong's political and media environment was governed under PRC sovereignty during his rule.
contrary_evidence: Authorities framed the measures as lawful enforcement of the National Security Law.

unresolved_gaps: Direct command-and-control, custody, and launch-discipline evidence is still thin.
Concrete arms-control follow-through beyond declaratory no-first-use language is limited.
Crisis de-escalation evidence in the Taiwan and Russia-Ukraine settings is mostly indirect.
Direct evidence of Xi personally authorizing or restraining specific military moves is thin.
Civilian-protection and operational-conduct evidence during the Taiwan crisis is limited.
Evidence of actual mediation or de-escalation in Russia-Ukraine remains mostly declaratory.
Water, sanitation, and local service-variation evidence is thin compared with health, pensions, housing, and crisis response.
Chain-of-command evidence for specific repression episodes remains limited.
Independent evidence on courts, legislatures, and oversight bodies resisting capture is thin.
Succession and term-limit mechanics could be more directly documented as a de facto transfer-rule breach.
Independent evaluation of implementation quality across provinces and local-government debt stress remains limited.
Distributional evidence beyond averages and poverty-lifted subgroups could be stronger.
Water/sanitation and housing-quality evidence is thinner than health, pensions, and child-welfare evidence.
Independent evaluation of service quality, regional equity, and front-line delivery remains limited.
Direct, ruler-specific evidence on Xi's own assets, gifts, family business interests, or beneficial ownership is missing.
Independent findings on concealment or obstruction tied personally to Xi are absent.
Evidence of truthful correction versus rhetorical anti-corruption messaging is weak.
Independent evaluation of whether loyalist-heavy appointments improved competence or mainly tightened political control is thin.
More subnational evidence on execution quality and correction would strengthen the adaptation story.
Durable causal impact of the COVID rollback and economic stabilization package remains under-audited.
